requirements.statement: Each title attribute of a form field, where it provides the field's label, lets the user know the exact function of that field.

citations.quote: Chaque attribut `title` permet-il de connaître la fonction exacte du champ de formulaire auquel il est associé ?
Retrouver dans le document les champs de formulaire dont l’étiquette est fournie par un attribut `title`

routes.statement: The content of the title attribute is relevant: it lets the user know the nature, type or format of the information the field expects.

citations.quote: Pour chaque champ de formulaire, vérifier que le contenu de l’attribut est pertinent
Texte à proximité du champ de formulaire permettant d’en connaître la nature, le type ou le format des informations attendues.

exceptions.statement: When the field also has aria-labelledby, aria-label or an associated <label>, the glossary's order of the accessible name makes that the field's label, and the title is not the one evaluated for relevance.

citations.quote: aria-labelledby ; Sinon aria-label ; Sinon <label> ; Sinon title.
Cet ordre doit être utilisé pour l’évaluation de la pertinence de l’étiquette

rationale.text: Relevance is judgment, so the entry is not full. The candidate is none, by decision Q48. The custom check looks at a native field whose only label mechanism is a title attribute with empty content: rendered, exposed and visible, with a title that is empty or only ASCII whitespace, no aria-labelledby or aria-label attribute, no associated <label> and no placeholder. It abstains on every other case, including every non-empty title, whose relevance is judgment. Its fault is evidence only. The wording asks about each title attribute associated with a field, but the methodology selects fields whose label is provided by a title attribute, and the glossary judges relevance on the source that actually labels the field, in the order of the accessible name. An empty title is present, but it does not give the field its label, so this test may not apply to such a field at all: on that reading the field has no label, which is a fault under test 11.1.1, not under this one. Codex contrasted it with an explicitly associated but blank <label for> under 11.2.1, which still gives a concrete associated element. Fabien chose to demote rather than rule (Q48). The link keeps its routes and its whole scope and becomes evidence_only; the check never answers no_fault, so its scope supports no positive result. What would raise the entry: a ruling that an empty title attribute is a label this test judges, with working fixtures where the title is the one effective source and where another source takes precedence. The only exception is the glossary's order of the accessible name, which puts aria-labelledby, aria-label and <label> before title; on a field that has one of them, the title is not the label evaluated, and the check abstains. The glossary also says that when title and placeholder are both present they must be identical. This test's wording and methodology do not state that rule, so nothing is claimed from it here; the check simply abstains when a placeholder is present. No axe rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment: whether a field's label is provided by its title turns on the order of the accessible name and on whether an empty attribute counts, which the text leaves open. Needs is empty: attributes, the DOM, styles and geometry are read on the page as loaded.

citations.quote: Chaque étiquette associée à un champ de formulaire est-elle pertinente (hors cas particuliers) ?
Le champ de formulaire possède un attribut `title` ;

lorsque l’attribut placeholder est présent, il est susceptible d’être restitué à la place de l’attribut title. Par conséquent, lorsque ces deux attributs title et placeholder sont présents, ils doivent être identiques.
Si c’est le cas pour chaque champ de formulaire, **le test est validé**.
